slices.focus: After shaky group nights, Tasha shifts to selective volunteer model with co-leaders and higher standards
slices.summary: The first full training round reveals that willingness does not equal readiness — two consecutive group nights feel 'thin and wobbly' as new facilitators freeze during silence or jump in with advice. Tasha responds by making the program more selective: clearer screening questions about handling ambiguity, paired co-leaders (every new facilitator with an experienced partner), higher coverage standards, and a deliberate slower growth pace. An experienced volunteer affirms the shift: 'I would rather mentor one good fit than keep rescuing a bad setup.' The agent helps Tasha frame this as 'building for steadiness, not just scale' and plan a one-page rationale linking screening, pairing, and coverage to stable group nights.
